payload.claim: `_describe_agent_event`'s docstring (line ~590) states "Every cell-authored field is scrubbed through `_scrub` before it reaches the returned line ... nothing else here is host-authored, so nothing else is exempt," but the `result` branch interpolates `event.get('num_turns')` (line 609) and `event.get('total_cost_usd')` (line 610) directly into the returned string, unscrubbed and unclipped. Both fields come from the same cell-authored `result` payload as `subtype`/`terminal_reason`, which two lines above *are* passed through `_scrub` — so a cell that sends either field as a string carrying control characters (rather than the number the SDK normally sends) reaches the rendered line whole, exactly the class of defect this spec exists to close (acceptance criterion 4), and exactly the branch the new tests (`test_every_cell_authored_field_is_clipped`, `test_an_agent_payload_cannot_put_control_characters_on_a_terminal`) never probe with an adversarial value for these two fields, which is why the gates did not catch it.
